rv.q: This ripping apart of Shakespeare's arguably most famous creation was a grounding adventure for me.
Still, it’s difficult to see the audience participation in Becoming Hamlet as much more than a gimmick.

An interesting experiment, this version of Hamlet must be considered a failure as it adds nothing to the understanding of the play and those not very familiar with the original text will not be able to follow it.

Hamlet struggles with justice and moral balance, while David H. Littleton’s Claudius fights to preserve his power, drawing the audience into their confrontation. Littleton, whose credits range from The Public Theater to Disney, is especially compelling in the “O, my offence is rank” soliloquy.
But the let's-all-play-Hamlet conceit proves to be more performative than profound.
Somewhere inside the production, there is an interesting perspective buried in its attempt to externalize Hamlet’s psychological conflict, but it never develops into a cohesive theatrical experience.
I simply found its central device more gimmick than revelation.

cn.t: An ambitious interactive experiment invites audiences to inhabit Hamlet, earning praise for its visceral immediacy but drawing criticism for uneven execution that doesn't fully deliver on its provocative premise.
